Description: Cancellation, deadlines and request-scoped values must propagate via context
Do: Take ctx as the first parameter of every blocking function
Don't: Use context.Background() inside libraries; ignore Done()
Code Good: func Fetch(ctx context.Context, id string) (*User, error) { ... }

Description: errgroup cancels siblings on first error and waits for all
Don't: Spawn raw goroutines without WaitGroup or cancellation
Code Good: g, ctx := errgroup.WithContext(ctx); g.Go(func() error {...}); g.Wait()
Code Bad: go func(){ doWork() }() // leaks on error

Description: Every goroutine must have a clear stop condition
Do: Always select on ctx.Done() in long-running goroutines
Don't: Spawn goroutines that block on unbuffered channels with no receiver

Description: Default http.Client is safe for concurrent use; per-request clients leak FDs
Do: Construct one http.Client per downstream as a singleton
Code Bad: resp, err := http.Get(url) // uses default sloppy client

Description: Default http.Client has no timeout; goroutines hang forever on a stuck server
Do: Set Timeout, plus per-Transport DialContext / TLS / ResponseHeader timeouts
Don't: Use http.DefaultClient unmodified for outbound calls

Description: Use fmt.Errorf with %w so callers can errors.Is / errors.As

Guideline: Define sentinel/typed errors at package boundary
Description: Callers should not parse error strings
Do: Export ErrNotFound or typed error structs implementing Unwrap

Description: Pin all deps via go.sum; vendor for reproducibility on air-gapped builds
Do: go mod tidy; go mod verify in CI
Code Good: go mod tidy && go mod verify

Description: Standard linters catch ~80% of common Go bugs
Do: Wire golangci-lint with staticcheck, errcheck, gosec, govet

Description: GC pressure dominates many Go service hot paths
Do: sync.Pool for byte buffers; bufio.Reader; pre-size slices via make([]T, 0, n)
Don't: Concatenate strings in loops; use 'fmt.Sprintf' for hot logging
Code Bad: s := ""; for _, x := range xs { s += x }

Do: Mount /debug/pprof on an internal port; 'go tool pprof' against prod

Description: Auth, tracing, metrics, retries belong in interceptors
Do: Chain unary + stream interceptors; OTel + prometheus + auth

Description: pgx is the fastest Postgres driver; works with database/sql or its own pool
Do: Use pgxpool for high-throughput; sqlc to generate type-safe SQL
Define tests as a slice of structs; sub-test via t.Run(name, ...)
Code Good: for _, tc := range cases { t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T){ ... }) }

Description: Cleans up resources without defer pyramids
Code Bad: defer srv.Close() // outside the test func
